name: E2E Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agent:
        description: 'Run a single agent (leave empty for all)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        options:
          - ''
          - claude-code
          - opencode
          - gemini-cli
          - factoryai-droid
          - cursor-cli
          - copilot-cli
          - roger-roger
          - codex
  push:
    branches:
      - main

# Concurrency: only one E2E job runs at a time
concurrency:
  group: e2e-tests
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Build the matrix dynamically so workflow_dispatch can select a single agent.
  matrix-setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
    steps:
      - id: set
        # Pass the input through env rather than interpolating it into the script:
        # `type: choice` only constrains the UI, so a REST-API dispatch could inject
        # shell metacharacters here otherwise.
        env:
          AGENT_INPUT: ${{ github.event.inputs.agent }}
        # gemini-cli is deliberately absent from the all-agents list. Since
        # Gemini CLI 0.57.0 the agent forces `core.hooksPath=''` on every shell
        # command it runs, so no checkpoint is recorded for a commit it makes and
        # the leg fails for a reason no change on our side can fix. It stays in
        # the workflow_dispatch choices above so the leg can be run by hand
        # against a newer Gemini release; put it back in this list (it is still
        # in the RED "reliable" tier in notify-slack) once one restores hooks.
        run: |
          input="$AGENT_INPUT"
          if [ -n "$input" ]; then
            echo "agents=[\"$input\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'agents=["claude-code","opencode","factoryai-droid","cursor-cli","copilot-cli","roger-roger","codex"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  e2e-tests:
    needs: matrix-setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      # Needed by the copilot-cli leg. GitHub does not allow matrix expressions in
      # `permissions:`, so this scope is granted to every leg's GITHUB_TOKEN. The
      # token is kept away from non-copilot agents in two ways: it is only placed
      # in COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN for the copilot-cli leg (see env blocks below), and
      # checkout runs with persist-credentials: false so it is not left in
      # .git/config for an agent process to read.
      copilot-requests: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        agent: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix-setup.outputs.agents) }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Don't persist the (copilot-scoped) GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config, where
          # an agent process running in the checkout could read it.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

      - name: Install agent CLI
        run: |
          case "${{ matrix.agent }}" in
            claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
            opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
            gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
            codex)       npm install -g @openai/codex ;;
            cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
            factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
            copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot  ;;
            roger-roger) ;; # installed by mise (see mise.toml)
          esac
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Verify roger-roger agent
        if: matrix.agent == 'roger-roger'

          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Verifying roger-roger binaries on PATH..."
          command -v roger-roger
          command -v entire-agent-roger-roger

        if: matrix.agent != 'roger-roger'
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}

        run: go run ./e2e/bootstrap

          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}

Only one job in that run fails: `e2e-tests (opencode)`. It's not a code regression — it's opencode hanging at startup.

## What the failure looks like

25 tests, all with the identical signature: `agent failed: signal: killed` at ~120.2s, which is opencode's own 2-minute per-prompt timeout (`e2e/agents/opencode.go:16`). Zero assertion failures — nothing tested a wrong value, every failure is a killed process.

24 of the 25 died on the **first** `opencode run` of their test, with literally empty stdout *and* stderr — opencode never printed even its `> build · claude-haiku-4-5` banner. The `entire` log for those tests shows no agent hook ever fired, so no session was ever started. The processes hung before doing anything.

## The tell is in the Bootstrap step

The warmup is a single, non-parallel `opencode run "say hi"`:

| run | warmup |
| --- | --- |
| 33801824229 (green, 09-03 20:23) | succeeded, ~12s |
| 33811795657 (red, 22:11) | **killed at 30s, empty output**; attempt 2 fine |
| 33838090646 (red, 09-04 04:48) | same |
| 33851433701 (red, 08:02) | same |

One process, no contention, cold directory → hang. Second attempt in the same directory → fast.

## Mechanism

`entire enable` writes `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` into every repo (confirmed in the failing tests' `git-tree.txt`). A local project plugin makes opencode run a per-directory `Npm.install()` of `@opencode-ai/plugin` and block `Plugin.init()` on `Config.waitForDependencies()` — no progress output, no timeout. That's anomalyco/opencode#47212 (and #33905, #31463, #30337, #44684). Every e2e test gets a fresh `/tmp/e2e-repo-*`, so every first prompt pays its own cold install.

## What I ruled out

- **Our code**: the only commits between the last green opencode run and the first red one are the trail-routing PR #2245.
- **A version bump**: opencode 1.18.27 in both green and red runs; runner image identical (`20260823.283.1`) between the green run and the first red one.
- **The Anthropic API**: the claude-code leg shares `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and got *faster* in the red run (311s → 268s).
- **Runner starvation**: `entire` hook perf was p50 4ms / p90 1.2s in the red run vs 10ms / 2.2s in the green one — the box was *less* loaded, consistent with dozens of processes blocked on the network rather than working.

## Two things on our side that make it worse

1. opencode registers no concurrency gate — codex/gemini/cursor are 2, copilot 4, droid 1, opencode unlimited — so all ~40 tests start at t=0.2s and each pays its own cold install at once.
2. 25 failures exceeds gotestsum's `--rerun-fails-max-failures=10`, so nothing was retried.

It's failed three runs straight (15/56, 29/56, 28/56 passing) and opencode is in notify-slack's RED "reliable" tier, so it will keep paging as a regression it isn't. The durable fix is to stop paying the npm install inside the timed prompt — pre-seed `.opencode/package.json`/`package-lock.json`/`node_modules` into each fresh test repo from one warmed template in `SetupRepo`, rather than letting the first prompt trigger it. Adding `RegisterGate("opencode", …)` would cut the pile-up but wouldn't fix the single-process 30s warmup hang. Want me to do either?
but any idea why this changed now it was green for a really long time
Good question — let me dig into what changed at that boundary.

Dug into that specifically — and the answer is that it **didn't** degrade gradually. It's a clean step change.

## The step

Bootstrap runs a single, non-parallel `opencode run "say hi"` before the suite. Its duration across every run I could pull:

| when | runs | bootstrap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-08-31 21:08 → 09-03 20:21 | 32 runs | **9–15s**, every one |
| 2026-09-03 22:10 onward | 3 runs | **40s**, every one (30s kill + 5s sleep + 5s retry) |

No creep, no flakiness beforehand. It flipped between 20:22 and 22:10 UTC on 09-03 and has stayed flipped.

Paired per-test timings across that boundary say the same thing:

```
TestEntireDisable                    5.4 →   5.2   (never invokes opencode)
TestHumanOnlyChangesAndCommits       5.3 →   5.3   (never invokes opencode)
TestModifyExistingTrackedFile       19.8 →  30.0
TestSingleSessionManualCommit       17.6 →  71.3
TestDirtyWorkingTree                26.3 → 118.2
TestResumeFromClonedRepo            31.5 → 114.3
                     median: 2.30× slower, +42s
```

Every test that starts opencode got ~20–30s per invocation slower. The two that never start it are unchanged to a tenth of a second. So it's inside opencode's startup, not the runner and not our code.

## What I ruled out

- **Our code** — only the trail-routing commits (#2245) are in that window; `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` hasn't changed since 08-17.
- **An opencode version bump** — 1.18.27 in both the green and red runs.
- **The runner image** — identical (`20260823.283.1`) across the green→red boundary, and a later image change didn't fix it.
- **The Anthropic API** — the claude-code leg shares the key and got *faster* (311s → 268s).
- **Machine load** — `entire` hook perf was p50 4ms / p90 1.2s in the red run vs 10ms / 2.2s green. The box was less busy, not starved.
- **The npm dependency tree** — plugin 1.18.25/26/27 all resolve to the same 26-package, 61MB tree; a cold-cache install measures 3s here; no publish burst (1–5/hour, steady), `@opentui/*` last published 09-01, plugin 1.18.27 on 09-02 — all before the boundary.
- **The binary download** — "Install agent CLI" is 1–2s in every run.

## What's left

Same binary, same repo, same image, same dependency content — so a service opencode calls during its startup got slow. I can't name which one: opencode's own logs (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/`) aren't in our artifacts, and it prints nothing while it waits, because #47212's `Config.waitForDependencies()`/plugin-init path has no timeout and no progress output.

Which is really the answer to "why now": nothing accumulated. The fragility was always there — a plugin-init path that can block forever and say nothing — but a 30s warmup budget and a 120s prompt budget had 10× headroom against a 10s startup. When startup went to 30s+, both budgets went to zero at once. That's why it looks like a cliff rather than a slide, and why it takes out half the suite instead of one test.

The cheap thing to fix first is our blindness to it: run opencode with `--print-logs --log-level DEBUG` and upload its log dir in the artifacts step. Next time this happens we'd have the actual stalled call instead of an empty stderr. Want me to do that, plus the `.opencode` pre-seed and the concurrency gate from before?

Every failure is `agent failed: signal: killed` at ~120.2s (opencode's own 2m per-prompt timeout in `e2e/agents/opencode.go`), with **zero assertion failures**. 24 of 25 died on the test's first `opencode run` with literally empty stdout AND stderr, and their `entire.log` shows no agent hook ever fired.

**It is a step change, not a creep.** The single-process bootstrap warmup (`opencode run "say hi"`) was 9–15s for all 32 runs back to 2026-08-31, then 40s (= 30s kill + 5s sleep + 5s retry) for every run after. Paired per-test timing across the boundary: median 2.30× slower / +42s for every test that invokes opencode; the two that never do (TestEntireDisable, TestHumanOnlyChangesAndCommits) are unchanged to a tenth of a second. So the added cost is inside opencode's startup.

Every e2e test gets a fresh `/tmp/e2e-repo-*`, so every first prompt pays it.

**Why it looks like a cliff:** nothing accumulated. A 30s warmup budget and 120s prompt budget had 10× headroom against a 10s startup; when startup went to 30s+, both hit zero at once.

**The blind spot to fix first:** opencode's own logs (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/`) are not in our artifacts and it prints nothing while stalled, so the actual stalled call cannot be named after the fact. Run it with `--print-logs --log-level DEBUG` and upload that dir.

Two aggravators on our side: opencode registers no `RegisterGate` (codex/gemini/cursor 2, copilot 4, droid 1), so ~40 tests launch at t=0.2s; and 25 failures exceeds gotestsum's `--rerun-fails-max-failures=10`, so nothing was retried. opencode is in notify-slack's RED "reliable" tier, so it pages as a regression it is not. ok, so what do you suggest

Three things, in this order. The theme is that we can't fix the cause, so fix the noise and fix our blindness — and don't build a mitigation until we know what's actually stalling.

**1. Stop it paging as a regression (now).** opencode is in notify-slack's `reliable` RED tier, so every push since Wednesday has fired a red alert for a cause that isn't ours. Move it to the yellow tier with a dated comment saying why, exactly like gemini-cli's existing carve-out in `matrix-setup`. E2E on main is push-triggered, not a merge gate, so nothing is actually blocked — the real cost right now is alert fatigue plus losing opencode coverage silently.

**2. Make the next occurrence diagnosable (same PR).** Two small changes:
- Upload `~/.local/share/opencode/log/` alongside `e2e/artifacts/` on the opencode leg. opencode writes those logs unconditionally; we just never collect them. That's the only reason I can't name the stalled call — it prints nothing to stderr while it waits.
- Raise the bootstrap warmup budget from 30s to 90s and log its duration. Right now attempt 1 gets SIGKILLed mid-way through whatever it's doing, which may be leaving state half-built for the tests that follow. A warmup that's allowed to finish is both a better warmup and a clean measurement of the startup cost.

**3. Then decide the mitigation — not before.** The obvious candidates are pre-seeding `.opencode/node_modules` into each test repo, an opencode concurrency gate, and a timeout bump. I'd hold all three, because my own measurement argues against the leading theory: a cold-cache `npm install` of the exact dependency tree takes **3 seconds** here, not 30. So #47212's npm path may be the wrong suspect, and pre-seeding would be a no-op we'd then have to maintain. One run with logs settles it.

If the logs show it's a hanging call to an opencode-operated service, the honest answer may be that there's no fix on our side and the gate/timeout is just headroom — worth knowing before writing code.

Want me to open that PR (tier move + log capture + warmup budget)? Separately, #47212 would be materially strengthened by our data — a deterministic 10s→30s step at a known timestamp, on Linux, same binary version, across 35 runs — but I won't post to it unless you say so.

Run finished — still red (27/56), but the log capture paid for itself immediately. We now have the stall pinpointed.

## The stall, exactly

opencode's own log ends mid-bootstrap. Killed warmup attempt:

```
10:24:17.741  loading path=/home/runner/work/cli/cli/.opencode/opencode.json
10:24:17.770  loading path=/home/runner/.opencode/opencode.json
10:24:17.772  loading path=/home/runner/.opencode/opencode.jsonc
              ← 90s of nothing, then SIGKILL
```

The successful retry crosses that same boundary in 91ms:

```
10:25:52.610  loading path=/home/runner/.opencode/opencode.jsonc
10:25:52.701  all LSPs are disabled
```

Across all 53 opencode processes in the run, **27 died inside that exact window** — last line a config `loading path=`, then nothing. The 26 that got through took a median of 2.8s but a p90 of 57.5s. opencode logs nothing at all about dependencies or installs (zero lines matching `npm|install|dependenc|node_modules`), which is why the artifacts named no cause. This is precisely the boundary #47212 describes.

Also worth knowing: **the stall is unbounded, not a fixed ~35s.** Attempt 1 burned the whole new 90s budget; attempt 2 took 4.8s. So raising the budget further is not a fix.

## What it's actually doing, measured locally

I reproduced it here. Whenever a local plugin file exists, opencode writes `.opencode/package.json` and installs **61MB / 27 packages** into that project directory:

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@opencode-ai/plugin": "1.18.15" } }
```

Two things about that pin. It follows **opencode's own binary version**, so every opencode release invalidates every repo's `.opencode/node_modules` and forces a fresh install in every project directory — and opencode ships roughly daily. And it is written **unconditionally**: I tested a variant of our plugin with `import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"` removed entirely, and the 61MB install still happened. The import isn't the trigger, the plugin file's existence is — so the tidy "drop the type-only import" fix is dead. Worth knowing before someone tries it.

Two implications past CI: every Entire user running opencode pays this on first launch in each repo — blank screen, no explanation — and again after each opencode upgrade. And our repo tracks `.opencode/package-lock.json` pinning `@opencode-ai/plugin: 1.4.7` from April, in a directory where opencode generates a `.gitignore` listing that exact filename. It's stale, it ships to every clone, and it's the same directory the warmup stalls in.

## What I'd do now

The pre-seed is no longer speculative, so I'd build it: at bootstrap, create one warmed `.opencode` by running `npm install @opencode-ai/plugin@<opencode version>` directly — 3s, bounded, and it actually reports failure — then copy `package.json`/`package-lock.json`/`node_modules` into each repo in `SetupRepo`. That takes the blocking install out of all ~40 test directories and out of the timed window, and it replaces the current warmup, which pays for a model round-trip to trigger an install as a side effect. I'd also drop the stale lockfile from tracking, and keep a concurrency gate on the list — I hit `database is locked` locally with just two concurrent opencode processes, so the global-DB contention is real too.

Note the 90s budget made bootstrap 138s instead of 78s for no gain; the explicit-install approach makes that moot, so I'd land them together rather than keep the bump on its own.

test(e2e): pre-build opencode's plugin deps instead of paying for them per repo

Whenever a project directory contains a local plugin file — which `entire
enable` always writes — opencode generates `.opencode/package.json`,
pinning `@opencode-ai/plugin` to its own binary version, and installs it
(27 packages, ~61MB) before it will finish bootstrapping. The install
runs inside a phase that logs nothing and has no timeout, so a slow one
is indistinguishable from a hang: the process sits between "loading
path=..." and "all LSPs are disabled" and produces no output at all.

Every test gets a fresh repo, so that install was being paid ~40 times
per run, in parallel. Since 2026-09-03 it stopped fitting in the budgets:
in run 33862929010, 27 of 53 opencode processes died inside that window.
Measured here, an unseeded directory takes 5m00.9s at 1% CPU to complete
an install that takes 3s when npm is invoked directly.

Build the tree once in Bootstrap, keyed by opencode version (the pin
follows the binary, so an upgrade invalidates it), and plant it in each
repo from a new RepoSeeder hook on SetupRepo. node_modules is symlinked
rather than copied: at ~61MB across thousands of small files and ~40
repos live at once, copying would cost about what it saves. The seed also
writes the same `.gitignore` opencode writes, which names its own file,
so nothing we plant is visible to git — these repos are the subject of
checkpoint assertions.

Measured with a seeded directory: bootstrap reaches the model in 839ms.

Every step degrades to today's behaviour rather than failing: no npm, an
unreadable version, or a platform without unprivileged symlinks all leave
the repo alone and let opencode install for itself.

Note this is not a test-only workaround. Every user running opencode pays
the same install on first launch in each repo, and again after each
opencode upgrade, with a blank screen and no explanation.

## What went in (`318d4f5b6`)

`Bootstrap` now builds the dependency tree opencode would otherwise install itself — once, keyed by opencode version, since the pin follows the binary and an upgrade invalidates it. A new `RepoSeeder` interface in `e2e/agents` (alongside the existing `ExternalAgent` one) lets `SetupRepo` plant it into each fresh repo, so opencode's blocking install never runs on the clock.

Three details worth flagging:

- **`node_modules` is symlinked, not copied.** ~61MB across thousands of small files × ~40 live repos — copying would cost roughly what it saves. I verified opencode reads through the link, leaves it in place, and still loads our plugin.

Half right — and the half that's wrong matters. I tested it four ways (opencode 1.18.15 locally, probing for a generated `.opencode/package.json`):

| project has | global plugins | install fires? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing | my 4 real ones | **no** |
| nothing | none | no |
| `.opencode/skills/` only | none | **no** |
| a non-Entire `.opencode/plugins/other.ts` | none | **yes** — 61MB tree |

So the trigger is specifically a **project-local plugin file** in `.opencode/plugins/`. Global plugins in `~/.config/opencode/plugins` don't cause it, and neither do project skills.

That splits your question in two:

- **Where you're right:** in a repo that already ships its own `.opencode/plugins/*.ts`, the toll is already there and Entire adds nothing.
- **Where it doesn't hold:** global plugins — which is where people actually keep personal plugins — buy no exemption. A developer with four global plugins pays nothing in any repo until `entire enable` writes a project-local one. Same for a repo with `.opencode/skills`.

Since very few repos ship their own opencode plugin, Entire is usually the thing that turns it on — per repo, and again after each opencode upgrade because the pin follows the binary version.

My earlier "every user running opencode pays this on first launch in each repo" was too broad; the accurate version is "every repo that didn't already contain a project-local opencode plugin, which is most of them." content.text:
That checkout answers it properly. The source says my "project-local plugin file" rule was too narrow.

## What actually arms it

`ConfigPaths.directories` (`packages/opencode/src/config/paths.ts:23`) returns the global config dir plus **every `.opencode` directory that exists**, walking up from cwd. `config.ts:452` then forks a background `@opencode-ai/plugin` install for *each* of them. `plugin/index.ts:184` is the gate:

```ts
if (plugins.length) yield* config.waitForDependencies()
```

and `waitForDependencies` (`config.ts:632`) joins those fibers with `concurrency: "unbounded"` and **no timeout** — the confirmed hang.

So the toll needs **two** things at once:

1. a project-local `.opencode` directory exists — the global dir's tree is installed once and reused across all projects, so it's the per-repo one that costs; and
2. at least one plugin is configured *anywhere*, global or project.

I re-tested against that rule and it holds — a repo with `.opencode/skills` and no project plugin, but my four **global** plugins present, installed in 3s:

| project | plugins | install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no `.opencode` | 4 global | no |
| `.opencode/skills` | none anywhere | no |
| `.opencode/skills` | 4 global | **yes** |
| `.opencode/plugins/other.ts` | none global | **yes** |

## So, your question

You're right for anyone who already has a project-local plugin, or a `.opencode` directory plus any global plugin — they already pay it and Entire adds nothing. Where it doesn't hold is global plugins on their own: those arm condition 2 but not condition 1, so a developer with four global plugins pays nothing in a repo with no `.opencode`. `entire enable` supplies **both** conditions in one step, and creating the directory is usually the half that was missing.

My earlier "project-local plugin file is the trigger" was one case of the rule, not the rule.

## Two other things worth having

**The 5min-vs-3s mystery is solved.** It isn't the npm CLI — `npm.ts:81` runs `@npmcli/arborist`'s `reify()` in-process. Same 27 packages, ~100× the wall time. That's why my direct `npm install` benchmark didn't reproduce it, and it's why the pre-seed works: reify over an existing lockfile plus `node_modules` is a fast no-op.

**"Why now" is still not opencode's code.** `git log` on `npm.ts`, `npm-config.ts`, `config.ts` and `plugin/index.ts` since Aug 25 shows exactly one commit, on 08-27 — nothing at the 09-03 boundary. That's now the third independent line of evidence pointing outside the binary.

One product option this surfaces, not a proposal: if Entire's plugin lived in `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` instead of `.opencode/plugins/`, the tree would be installed once globally and no repo would get a project `.opencode` — the toll disappears rather than being pre-paid. The tradeoff is that a global plugin loads in every project, including ones where Entire was never enabled, so it's a real design call rather than a relocation.

Bootstrap looked fixed — deps built in 4.9s, warmup passed first try in 8.6s — but the tests still failed, slightly worse than before (22/56). The opencode logs showed **31 of 53 processes still dying in the install window**, median stall 23.5s.
